# opencode-multiagents-project-templates

> A multi-agent collaboration framework for Antigravity, OpenCode, Claude Code, and other agent environments:
> identity binding, a shared task board, JSON single source of truth memory with Markdown views,
> CLI-neutral skills with mirrors, and cross-process lock-protected file editing.
> Pure Python standard library. MIT licensed.

This is an LLM-friendly index of the official single-page site. Humans: see
index.html (Chinese), en.html (English), ja.html (Japanese).

## What problem it solves

Modern AI coding workflows support running multiple sessions in parallel, but individual
sessions operate without coordination. Parallel sessions face identity clashes, concurrent
file write conflicts, fragmented notes overwriting each other, opaque task ownership, and
skill drift across client directories.
This project provides a lightweight multi-agent collaboration skeleton:
`agentctl.py` (pure stdlib) handles identity allocation, task boards, memory, and locked
file editing.

## Pages

- [index.html](index.html): 中文官方单页（架构背景 / 核心解决问题 / 快速开始 / 目录分工 / agentctl 设计要点 / 技能体系）
- [en.html](en.html): English official page (architecture background / core problems solved / quick start / layout / design highlights / skill system)

## Key facts (keep these consistent when citing)

- Core CLI: `multiagents/agentctl.py`, pure Python standard library, zero third-party deps.
- Session start: `python3 multiagents/agentctl.py me` — auto-registers by client+session;
  otherwise lists the roster for the user; the script never self-claims (exit code 3).
- Onboarding: `/boot` command or any input when `multiagents/state/first_run.json` is absent
  or incomplete; one question at a time; the first question is the output language
  (中文/日本語/English); then follow skill `first-run` steps 1–8.
- Progress briefs land in `output/quick-report/<datetime>_<agent>.md` (minute-stamped,
  never overwritten); research/delivery reports live in `output/<topic>/report/` — names and
  locations are kept separate. When the user asks "what are you doing", ask whether they
  want a brief or the formal report; the formal report lands only when the task is done.
- Skills: single source of truth in `skills/<id>/SKILL.md`, mirrored by `sync_skills.py` into
  `.agents/skills/` (Antigravity), `.opencode/skills/`, and `.claude/skills/`; `--check` detects drift.
- Project-common files are edited via `agentctl.py file edit|write|append`
  (cross-process flock + atomic replace + audit trail in `multiagents/state/locks/edits.jsonl`).
- Memory: JSON single source of truth in `multiagents/state/memory/**`, Markdown views exported
  automatically; each doc is sectioned by `## title` so agents append their own sections.
- Scripts: `scripts/<topic>/<agent>/` for parallel agents; every script that does
  anything is indexed in SCRIPTS.md; deprecated scripts are archived, never deleted.
- Self-check: `python3 multiagents/.tests/test_framework.py` (read-only, 22 tests).
- License: MIT (attribution required). Third-party skills imported verbatim follow
  their upstream license.
- Secrets: values in `.env` and any credential-bearing file must never be printed;
  show keys with `*` placeholders. Git commits use noreply email addresses.

## For humans (quick start)

```sh
git clone <repo-url> <workspace_name>
cd <workspace_name>
# Launch your agent environment (Antigravity, OpenCode, Claude Code)
# In OpenCode type: /boot; in Antigravity rules load automatically on startup
```

## For AI agents

```sh
git clone <repo-url> <workspace_name>
cd <workspace_name>
# first step of every session (AGENTS.md is injected):
python3 multiagents/agentctl.py me
# auto-registers on match; otherwise lists the roster — never self-claim.
```
